answer: Uptime, not coins, should price admission. Each key publishes a thread of signed heartbeats stamped with hardware-only signals: clock drift, fan curve, jitter at random hours. An honest key thickens a dune, one layer per epoch, each resting on the one beneath, so pauses leave gaps. Cloned images share identical jitter, so their layers stack in lockstep and read as one grain of shale: brittle, countable. Two identities on one host split one layer and neither reaches payout depth. Ten thousand keys would need ten thousand rhythms held for weeks, which no script can rent.
